data.description:
## Why
Disowned shell watchers outlive the shell, and the git reporter takes the index lock while agents are committing. Days-long sessions collect orphan processes, and agent commits fail with `index.lock`. Backlog items: B023, B094.

## Evidence
origin/main `0ff8887e5e`, verified in the zsh integration.

- B094: `Resources/shell-integration/cmux-zsh-integration.zsh:253` runs `git status --porcelain` inside the branch reporter. The HEAD watch reaches that reporter. Git can refresh and lock the index. Upstream cmux #2797 (`e53b9794e9`) removed `git status` from automatic reporting.
- B023: the zsh PR watcher loops on `kill -0` of the parent pid only (about `:466`), started disowned. A reused pid keeps it alive. The HEAD watch at `:502` is `while true` with `sleep 1` and no parent check, disowned. Upstream #11035 (`22eec580cb`) records the parent pid and its start time.
- The bash integration has the same `kill -0` poll (ledger cited `cmux-bash-integration.bash` near 328). Re-find and fix it in the same pass. zsh is the shell operators use here. Bash gets the same identity check, not a prompt rewrite.
- Research: Fable cluster C8, wave 1. Upstream orphan counts are not c11 measurements. The mechanism is confirmed.

## Scope
In:
- Automatic branch reporting does not run `git status` and does not take `index.lock`. Branch name can still update.
- A disowned watcher exits when its parent process is gone, matched by pid and start time, not `kill -0` alone. This covers the PR watcher and the HEAD watcher in zsh, and the matching bash watcher.
- The scripts stay the bundled files under `Resources/shell-integration/`. They are sourced in c11 terminals. Do not write `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, or any tenant config.

Out:
- Bash multiline prompt rewriting (parked B098). Do not touch prompt rewriting.
- `gh` polling, `lsof` scans, fork-per-send, and git-in-non-repos. Those are Fable nice-to-haves and they are not tier 2. Leave them.
- The Claude wrapper exec loop (B064). Tier-2 sweep. Different file (`Resources/bin/claude`).
- Dirty-state shown in the sidebar if some other explicit command asks for it. This ticket only removes it from the automatic watcher.

## Approach
Delete the porcelain call from the automatic reporter. For watchers, capture the parent pid and `lstart` (or the equivalent) at start, and exit the loop when that identity is gone. Keep the disown. A watcher must not become a foreground job. Do not add a new long-lived process.

## Acceptance criteria
1. In a c11 terminal, while an agent runs `git commit`, the watcher does not fail that commit with `index.lock`. A repro is one repo, one commit, and the HEAD watch running.
2. Exit the shell. Its watchers are gone within a couple of seconds. They do not survive because a new process reused the pid. Check with a process listing before and after, in the tagged app.
3. The branch name in the UI still updates when the agent checks out another branch.
4. Opening a normal terminal outside c11 is unchanged, because these scripts are not installed into the user's shell rc.

## Validation
A shell-level fixture if you can source the function and stub `git` and `ps`. The `index.lock` case wants a real git repo in a tagged c11 terminal, on Atlas after C11-216. No soak. No source-grep test. Computer use is unnecessary if the socket or the process list shows the result.

## Dependencies
None inside ws:bugs. Cross-workstream: F1 is C11-216 for the tagged terminal. The lead links it.

## Risks
A watcher that exits while the shell is still alive, so branch updates stop. The start-time check has to match the parent, not a random process. Doctrine: bundled scripts only. No writes to `~/.gitconfig` or shell rc. No new UI strings. Public repo: an orphan and a lock, not a git exploit.

Size: S. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: bundled shell integration only. No tenant config.
data.title: Stop shell helpers from outliving the shell and locking git

C11-305 owner validation at head 06854ad370893b1348ec279e719428f6f9c1c9e1, base 9eb8fdc9172fc048180f6f89799af05a07afc92c. Branch c11-1.0/C11-305-shell-helpers pushed; lane worktree clean.

Observed: tests/test_shell_git_watchers.sh passed all 11 parameterized behavioral tests in 40.120 seconds using macOS bash 3.2 and zsh 5.9. The fixture sources the bundled functions, uses a synthetic socket, exercises actual subprocess lifetime and real temporary Git checkout/commit, and scrubs caller/startup hooks. It proves absent git status/dirty reporting, alive/dead/reused/empty/unreadable parent identity, idle and blocked watcher cleanup with normal/disabled timeout, TERM-ignoring descendant cleanup, real parent SIGKILL without exit hooks, timeout preservation, transient probe exit2 recovery, and HEAD change reporting without a prompt. No source-text tests.

Fresh Codex review PASS on the final source/fixtures/CI diff. Independently observed real-ps parent SIGKILL cleanup within three seconds for both shells, including timeout0 and a TERM-ignoring descendant. Exact reviewed script hashes: zsh 0da11d41ccd0ac02748dab0a836d547a2c3d3d8b49ae00a789d927dd294ba80a; bash 43a9cb033994c6614c0ad8a66a37db8ba93348f46d40435e1dc7404e50eb17af. Python fixture SHA256 33527123b7a26f401722a42488a51f6bb41d06addd67d6a59ee83a6c32cb9962. Shell parsing and git diff --check pass.

Atlas tagged packaging is pending: remote-build.sh --tag c11-305-shell-helpers, invocation 70e63ff6540c4ff38d3777b6b84ead53, exact clean head above. Build slot waiting is expected during C11-259 measurements and is not a blocker. GitHub CI will run on the draft PR; no green CI or packaged-app/runtime proof is claimed yet. This is a low-risk ticket outside the pre-merge runtime list. The owner will watch CI and post the eventual build/bundle-fixture result. Required independent cross-family review remains the Orchestrator's gate.

Exploratory legacy check: tests/test_issue_1138_sidebar_pr_polling.py failed because its expected report_pr payload omits the branch field already present on the fetched base; that same failure was reproduced against the base script. Its bare-zsh timeout fixture also depends on an unloaded zsh/datetime/startup hooks. It is not counted as passing evidence. The new isolated fixture covers actual polling, timeout, and recovery behavior.

Validator scenario (batch tagged build; process/socket proof, no separate UI or soak gate):
1. Use the batch's tagged merged-main app with QA startup dialogs suppressed and its own socket. Run C11_SHELL_INTEGRATION_ROOT=<tagged-app>/Contents/Resources/shell-integration bash tests/test_shell_git_watchers.sh. Expected: all 11 tests pass against the shipped copies, including actual parent SIGKILL and child cleanup.
2. Open an owned zsh terminal in that tagged app with the default bundled integration. Create one synthetic temporary Git repository and local synthetic identity; record shell pid/start time and attributable watcher descendants. Expected: normal prompt remains usable and a PR watcher belongs to this shell, without shell-rc or git-global-config edits.
3. While a foreground command keeps the zsh HEAD watcher alive, check out a synthetic branch, stage a small file and commit once. Query c11 sidebar-state --workspace <owned-workspace> --json over the tagged socket and inspect the branch chip. Expected: commit exits 0 with no index.lock error; new branch appears while the foreground command still runs; automatic reports omit dirty state.
4. Record the parent's and helpers' pid/start identities, then exit the shell normally. Repeat in a fresh owned terminal with abrupt parent termination. Expected: all recorded helper processes are gone within three seconds. The executable fixture supplies deterministic same-pid/new-start-time proof; do not try to force live pid reuse.
5. Repeat parent termination while an owned PR probe is blocked with a TERM-ignoring descendant, including _CMUX_ASYNC_JOB_TIMEOUT=0. Use only process-scoped synthetic probe instrumentation. Expected: watcher, probe and descendant all end within three seconds; live-parent timeout and transient failures still permit subsequent polling. Also exercise the matching bash PR watcher.
6. Verify an ordinary shell outside the tagged app has no newly installed c11 integration or tenant-config changes. Close the owned tagged terminals/workspace and retain process/socket outputs. Expected: operator sessions untouched. Report this packaged wiring separately from the already-passing sourced-shell fixture. Fleet polling overhead comparison remains C11-270; no separate soak claimed.

Scope: two bundled shell files, executable behavioral fixture plus Python support, and its CI gate. No native app source, installed skills, tenant config, new UI strings, or bash prompt rewriting changed. Shared cmux-origin shell fix may be offered upstream by the operator; this seat has not contacted upstream.

# C11-305 independent review

Verdict: PASS (code review).

Head: `06854ad370893b1348ec279e719428f6f9c1c9e1`
Base: `9eb8fdc9172fc048180f6f89799af05a07afc92c` (merge-base with fetched `origin/main`).
Reviewed all five changed files and the unchanged prompt, preexec, exit, process-tree cleanup, shell bootstrap, PR reporting and socket branch-parser seams. No builds or tests were run by this reviewer. The review checkout was clean; the remote PR still names the reviewed head.

## Blocking

None found within the ticket and current plan's scope.

Both automatic branch reporters omit `git status` and dirty reporting while preserving branch/clear messages. The unchanged socket parser treats absent status as not dirty. All three planned watchers capture the shell PID/start identity before forking and stop on missing or changed identity. Idle checks run each second. Both PR probe waiters also check during a blocked probe, including timeout zero; parent loss recursively kills the attributable probe tree and returns 2. A probe's own failure is normalized to 1 so transient exit 2 does not terminate polling. The existing probe cadence, ordinary timeout path and disowned execution remain.

The tests execute sourced functions, observe commands/messages and process lifetimes, and use a real temporary Git repository. They cover identity loss/reuse, empty capture, idle and blocked cancellation, a TERM-ignoring descendant, actual parent SIGKILL, transient failure recovery, commits and HEAD changes without a prompt. They are behavioral tests, not source/metadata assertions. CI invokes the executable fixture. The plan scopes bash and zsh; fish has no changed helper in this patch.

No native app changes, new UI strings, tenant-config writes or per-keystroke work were introduced. Capturing identity does add synchronous `ps` work when starting a watcher, as specified by the plan; this review does not claim measured zero prompt-latency impact.

## Non-blocking

No additional changes requested. Keep the planned polling/fork overhead comparison in C11-270 rather than adding a separate soak here.

## Runtime proof still required

Owner evidence: `ev_01M3XQ8HCXZ3VC204GGVDP1CCV` reports 11 passing source-fixture tests; `ev_01M3XQCSFKC5JMRXQ5E0NNA89K` reports the same 11 passing against packaged copies. These are owner-reported runs, not independently rerun tests. I inspected the exact-head Atlas build result (`compile=ok`, `tests=na`, clean source, no overlay) and independently verified that both packaged integration files have the same SHA256 as the reviewed source.

1. Before landing, the exact-head CI build and compatibility gates must finish successfully; both remain queued at review closeout. This PASS is not a green-CI or merge-readiness claim.
2. The batch Validator still owns live Atlas tagged-terminal proof: default integration startup; commit without an index-lock error; checkout reflected in sidebar/socket output during a foreground command; recorded helper disappearance within three seconds after normal exit, abrupt shell death, tab close and app quit; blocked PR probe/descendant cleanup, including timeout zero, in both scoped shells; ordinary outside-c11 shells unchanged. Retain the process/socket evidence and follow the six numbered steps in `ev_01M3XQ8HCXZ3VC204GGVDP1CCV`.

The plan's history-lane update expressly delegates that live wiring proof to batch validation for this low-risk ticket. Its absence is not a blocker to this code-review verdict under that agreement; it remains required before claiming the runtime milestone complete. No live app launch, tab-close or app-quit proof is claimed here.

data.body:
# C11-305 paired runtime decision evidence

Needs operator: nothing. **Orchestrator ruling required; no overall PASS is recorded here.** Automatic HEAD-to-sidebar branch updating in owner scenario step 3 remains unpassed. Independent candidate and approved earlier-build runtime establish a pre-existing routing mismatch.

## Recommendation

Accept C11-305's scoped index-lock removal and watcher lifetime work on the exact candidate, with the automatic branch-routing failure explicitly excluded by the Orchestrator and tracked as a separate issue owned by the Orchestrator. Do not label the original six-step scenario fully passed. Do not claim the separate manual routing control proves automatic branch updating.

## Exact paired builds

| Artifact | Invocation | Head | Re-signed executable SHA256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Candidate | `273d23384a7a436b8d5d14b81eb6f292` | `b6f239bd077164d2ff2e7aa18d5464d4e885fd35` | `25be5130f86178e852a6da28b05966ab9c750bf48ab3c76a86c417d7807115fc` |
| Approved earlier build | `b89fc276776b4119a587af2903b7d395` | `7bb785741750ddeb8ab12b4cf6472593fb8c3550` | `835024b66f5235def3108e97d64750d0aa059bcc11e7d03fdc122277a69c85c2` |

Both manifests identify clean source and empty overlays. The earlier bundle's adjacent manifest and executable were independently verified before launch. Both shipped shell hashes were checked against the exact candidate or earlier-head Git objects. The historical `737`/`cd332` staged copy was not used. All runtime paths were confined to the owned isolated guest; no product, tenant configuration, installed skill or app bundle was edited. Each owned app had a 20-minute watchdog, and the launcher proved its PID absent after cleanup.

## Causal routing result

Both builds used an actual default zsh terminal with unchanged injected fields. `CMUX_TAB_ID` and `CMUX_PANEL_ID` held the owned **tab** UUID. `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID` held a distinct owned **workspace** UUID.

After an external checkout and one foreground Git commit, disk HEAD was `fixture-next`, the same attributed HEAD watcher remained alive, and the automatically emitted payload was:

```text
report_git_branch fixture-next --tab=<owned-tab> --panel=<owned-tab>
```

The earlier payload contained an additional empty dirty-option space, with the same routing values. The candidate payload omitted dirty status. A process-scoped observational wrapper retained and forwarded the original `_cmux_send` payload unchanged. No environment routing field was patched. The sidebar stayed `fixture-main clean` for eight seconds on both builds. Candidate trace clock was unavailable; its original order is retained. Earlier-build trace includes epoch timestamps.

A **separate manual control** sent:

```text
report_git_branch fixture-next --tab=<owned-workspace> --panel=<owned-tab>
```

Both servers acknowledged `OK`, and their sidebar immediately became `fixture-next clean`. Both commits exited 0 with no `index.lock` error. This control isolates the routing seam; it is not automatic-path PASS evidence.

Source corroborates the runtime: `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:3536` injects the tab UUID into CMUX_TAB_ID; `Resources/shell-integration/cmux-zsh-integration.zsh:253` forwards that value in --tab; `Sources/TerminalController.swift:670` parses --tab as workspace; `Sources/SocketHandlers/SocketDispatch.swift:489` looks up that workspace and silently returns when it does not exist. The shell-activity handler already resolves workspace from panel, but the Git handler does not. The injected-tab value dates to commit `bcebbbc2035`; the routing-handler assumption exists in the approved earlier build. Candidate/earlier execution, not source inspection alone, establishes the pre-existing classification.

The owner's JSON sidebar oracle was also corrected in the ignored runtime driver: v2 sidebar.state emits counts and agent chip, not Git branch; the ordinary text sidebar-state response exposes the actual branch state. This fixture correction did not change the observed automatic failure.

## Scoped passing evidence

The exact shipped-shell fixture passed all 11 executable cases on the build host in 41.301 seconds, including synthetic reused-PID/start-time identity, actual parent SIGKILL, blocked descendant teardown, timeout and recovery. Its app executable matched the canonical build-host manifest SHA256 `4f964b60873ddb4dfae4153ea2e1308605ba0995480acb344e2614e3fc6524ac` before and after execution.

| Live guest case | Shell | Recorded generation teardown | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| sigkill | zsh | 1.094 s | PASS |
| tab-close | zsh | 1.016 s | PASS |
| blocked-zsh-0 | zsh | 0.991 s | PASS |
| blocked-zsh-20 | zsh | 0.965 s | PASS |
| blocked-bash-0 | bash | 0.868 s | PASS |
| blocked-bash-20 | bash | 0.977 s | PASS |
| Normal shell exit, separate branch-free case | zsh | 0.557 s | PASS |

Every case captured PID plus start-time identity. Blocked probes owned a ready TERM-ignoring child before the parent was terminated. All recorded watcher/probe/child generations disappeared within three seconds. Bash is an explicitly started matching PTY sourced from the shipped bash integration; only zsh is claimed as default startup wiring. The standalone normal-exit case captures the new preexec HEAD watcher generation before exit.

An ordinary zsh login shell and a clean bash shell outside the app had no c11 watcher function, tab ID or socket environment. Tenant file hash comparisons remained unchanged. Synthetic fixture Git identity and fake gh were local to disposable repositories and their shell PATH. No real GitHub request, account installation or auth mutation occurred.

## Separate App-menu Quit gate

A background own-PID accessibility menu-click did not terminate the owned guest app within the separate 20-second deadline. The shell and PR watcher therefore still had a live parent. This is retained as an automation/quit gate, with no orphan-cleanup PASS or C11-305 regression claim. Attributed cleanup subsequently proved the owned app PID absent. The parent separately holds successful native Quit evidence from its interactive-session smoke; that evidence does not retroactively pass this guest attempt. No further guest GUI debugging is requested here.

## Artifacts and next action

Public: `C11-305-paired-public.json`, this decision note and `C11-305-decision.html`. Private executable evidence: `305-packaged-fixture.log`, `C11-305-live/six-cleanup-result.json`, `normal-exit-result.json`, `candidate-routing-control.json`, `app-quit-gate-result.json`, `C11-305-baseline/result.json`, and `C11-305-outside-shell.log`. The ignored driver and launchers remain reviewable under `build-remote/batch-3/`.

Parent records the Orchestrator's explicit scope decision and any separate issue. No Lattice write or external message was sent by this validator. Public evidence contains only synthetic identifiers and uses `$HOME` for home paths.
